title: Morning Headlines
intro: A potential US-Iran peace deal dominates the day as diplomatic breakthroughs and clean-energy milestones round out a consequential Friday.

items.title: Pakistan declares 'final, agreed text' of US-Iran peace deal reached as US downs Iranian drones
items.subtitle: CBS News / ABC News
items.summary: Pakistan's prime minister announced that negotiators have agreed on a final text to end the US-Iran war that began in February 2026, with Iran committing to never develop nuclear weapons in exchange for sanctions relief and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz; US forces shot down multiple Iranian attack drones in the same hours, underscoring the fragility of the moment.

items.title: EU unblocks Ukraine and Moldova membership talks after Hungary drops veto
items.subtitle: Euronews / The Washington Post
items.summary: EU ambassadors unanimously agreed to open the first cluster of accession negotiations with Ukraine and Moldova, with formal talks set for June 15 in Luxembourg; the breakthrough follows Hungary lifting its two-year veto after Kyiv agreed to a minority-rights action plan, marking the most significant step yet toward Ukraine's eventual EU membership.

items.title: World's first large-scale hydrogen engine feeds electricity into a national grid
items.subtitle: Euronews
items.summary: A pure-hydrogen combustion engine built by Finland's Wärtsilä successfully supplied power to Spain's national grid — a world first for large-scale hydrogen power generation — demonstrating a potential solution to the intermittency problem that has limited renewable energy expansion.

items.title: Oil falls toward $85 on Iran deal hopes; equities gain ahead of first Warsh Fed decision
items.subtitle: Charles Schwab / Bloomberg
items.summary: Crude oil dropped roughly 2% as traders priced in an imminent reopening of the Strait of Hormuz; global equity markets extended gains on the same optimism ahead of Wednesday's Federal Reserve rate decision, the first chaired by new Chair Kevin Warsh, where a rate increase is widely expected after last week's stronger-than-expected jobs report.

items.title: Poland's F-35 'Hussarz' jets officially enter service with ceremonial flyover of major cities
items.subtitle: Euronews
items.summary: Poland formally commissioned its first three F-35A stealth fighters at Łask Air Base, followed by a flypast over Warsaw, Gdańsk, Kraków, and Łódź; the jets, nicknamed 'Hussarz,' are part of a 32-aircraft, $4.6 billion order and mark a major step in reinforcing NATO's eastern flank.
